name: Nineveh under Nahum
charge: A bloody city, full of lies and robbery, whose prey departeth not; the dwelling of the lions that filled his holes with prey; the wicked counsellor that imagineth evil against the Lord
summary: Nahum’s burden of Nineveh declares the Lord jealous and avenging, slow to anger but never clearing the guilty, and names the wicked counsellor who came out of Nineveh imagining evil against Him (Nahum 1:1-3; Nahum 1:11). The lions’ den that had emptied Jacob would be flooded, spoiled and left empty, and the bloody city, full of lies and robbery, would have no healing for its wound (Nahum 2:2-13; Nahum 3:1; Nahum 3:19). The teachers read it as the fall of Nineveh in 612 BC and, in several classes, as the sentence on Mystery Babylon, America.
offenseFull: The burden opens with who the Lord is: jealous, avenging, taking vengeance on His adversaries and reserving wrath for His enemies (Nahum 1:2). God reserves wrath for America, for China, for Europe, the class says, for what they did to our people. He is slow to anger and great in power and will not at all acquit the wicked (Nahum 1:3); somebody tell the white man, one teacher says. His way is in the whirlwind and the storm, and one teaching sees Him in today’s hurricanes and earthquakes; the mountains quake before Him, and none can stand before His indignation (Nahum 1:3-6).

Nineveh had been spared once. The Lord held off because His people were there, the Luke 11 teaching says, and the Empires class says Jonah stayed the destruction but Nineveh did not change the people there, which was us, and eventually Nineveh fell. Tobit, a captive of Naphtali there, saw the bodies of Israelites thrown out about the walls of Nineveh (Tobit 1:17-18); the Assyrians did much wickedness to our people, the teacher says. The emptiers had emptied Jacob and marred his branches (Nahum 2:2). Nineveh was the den of the lions, where the lion tore enough for his whelps and filled his holes with prey (Nahum 2:11-12). Out of her came one who imagined evil against the Lord, a wicked counsellor (Nahum 1:11); one class says that is America, another a system of people (Daniel 7:8).

Woe to the bloody city, full of lies and robbery, whose prey never departs (Nahum 3:1). Woe to the bloody city, this is America, one class says, and the heaps of carcasses are our forefathers. Another says the bloody city robbed our lands, our identity, our culture, even our minds, and we are the prey that is still here; the study note on Exodus 14 reads the prey that does not depart as the people in captivity who will not leave. She was the well-favoured harlot, mistress of witchcrafts, who sold nations through her whoredoms (Nahum 3:4), which one class reads as the harlot Mystery Babylon (Revelation 17:5).
judgmentFull: The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble, and knows those who trust Him (Nahum 1:7): trouble is coming, the class says, and the Lord is good in the day of trouble if you keep the law, and we will have to depend on each other. With an overrunning flood He would make an utter end of the place, and affliction would not rise a second time (Nahum 1:8-9); one teacher sets it with Babylon, which shall not rise again (Jeremiah 51:64). He would break the yoke from off Judah and burst the bonds (Nahum 1:13): God will break the yoke of the white man and the nations off of us, the class says. No more of Nineveh’s name would be sown, her images would be cut off, and He would make her grave (Nahum 1:14), which one teaching reads of Esau (Isaiah 14:20). To Judah it was good tidings on the mountains: keep your solemn feasts (Nahum 1:15).

The one who dashes in pieces came up; the chariots raged in the streets, the gates of the rivers were opened and the palace dissolved, and though they cried stand, stand, none looked back; she was empty, void and waste (Nahum 2:1-10). The Lord of hosts was against her (Nahum 2:13; Nahum 3:5). Her shepherds would slumber and her bruise would have no healing, and all who heard of her fall would clap their hands, for her wickedness had passed on everyone continually (Nahum 3:18-19).

The history teachings give the fall: Babylon and the Medes teamed up to take down the Assyrian, Cyaxares the Mede with Nabopolassar, in 612 BC after about three months of siege; the Median army stormed the city and left ruined hills and heaps of debris, and by 600 BC Assyria was gone. Tobit had told his son to leave Nineveh, because what Jonas the prophet spoke would surely come to pass, and before he died he heard of its destruction and rejoiced (Tobit 14:4; Tobit 14:8; Tobit 14:15). The Disturbing Truth class reads Nahum 1 as not about ancient Assyria but about Babylon and her allies, and the other classes read the bloody city as Mystery Babylon: Nineveh and America are one and the same, one teacher says.

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Deceit and fraud a characteristic of the wicked.
Witchcraft, wizardry, and sorcery condemned and forbidden to be practice.
Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.
You shall not steal another's property.
